submission.note: GEMSDOE66 unique multi-scale structural convergence field, continuous probability (not dots), coherence+lineament+curvature fusion; format-valid, no organizer score claimed

hypothesis: Subtle faults not in the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue produce multi-scale structural convergence: convergent lineament orientations, alternating convex/concave curvature at multiple scales, and elevated structural grain within fault zones. A fused coherence x lineament-density x curvature field targets this signature.
mechanism: Multi-scale structural convergence field computed from footprint geometry (disclosed synthetic surrogate since the 1 m GeoDAWN DEM is unreachable). Three curvature scales (3/7/15 cells), structure-tensor orientation coherence (2 scales), directional lineament density (4 strikes), fused into continuous [0,1] probability, sparse emission at top 40,000 cells.
physical_signature: distributed fault-zone deformation — convergent lineaments + multi-scale curvature + structural grain
named_non_fault_mimic: alluvial-fan distributary networks and drainage antecedence can produce convergent lineaments and curvature
why_catches_missing_faults: targets subtle structural convergence rather than sharp scarps (LIDAR-01 lane), sparse dots (K66C/H67-1 lanes), or geophysics/topography alone (H67 lane); catches faults too subtle for scarplet templates and too structured for geophysics-only fields
differs_from_repo: continuous field (not dots), multi-scale structural operators (not single-scale scarplet), structural/topographic only (no inventory layers, no geophysics-only), sparse top-K emission instead of Poisson-disk dots

leakage_canary.detail: no trained model, no withheld truth available; field is a disclosed synthetic surrogate
